source.original_text: Let M⊆E and M′⊆E′ be embedded submanifolds of finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces, let F:M→M′ be smooth, and let F̄ be any smooth ambient neighborhood extension. For every x∈M, the manifold differential is DF(x)=D F̄(x)|_{TₓM}. Consequently it is linear, depends on a representing curve only through its base point and velocity, and is independent of the extension: any second extension F̂ gives D F̄(x)[v]=D F̂(x)[v] for v∈TₓM.

lean.statement: ∀ (E V : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [NormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedSpace ℝ V] (s : Set E) (f g : E → V) (c : ℝ → E) (t₀ : ℝ) (v : E), DifferentiableAt ℝ f (c t₀) → DifferentiableAt ℝ g (c t₀) → HasDerivAt c v t₀ → (∀ᶠ t in 𝓝 t₀, c t ∈ s) → (f =ᶠ[𝓝[s] (c t₀)] g) → fderiv ℝ f (c t₀) v = fderiv ℝ g (c t₀) v

blind_reconstruction.text: Let E and V be arbitrary real normed vector spaces, let s be any subset of E, let f and g be functions from E to V, let c be a function from the real numbers to E, let t₀ be a real number, and let v belong to E. Suppose that f and g are each Fréchet differentiable at c(t₀), that c is differentiable at t₀ with derivative v, that c(t) belongs to s for every t in some neighborhood of t₀, and that there is a neighborhood U of c(t₀) such that f(x) = g(x) for every x in U ∩ s. Then the Fréchet derivatives of f and g at c(t₀), applied to v, are equal: Df(c(t₀))[v] = Dg(c(t₀))[v].

import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Deriv.Comp

/-!
# Extension-independent derivatives along feasible curves

The relative germ of an ambient map determines its derivative on every actual
velocity of a curve locally in the feasible set. This is the explicit
extension-independence step following Boumal §3.4 Proposition 3.35. The general
normed-space interface does not define a manifold tangent space or identify
the complete manifold differential.
-/

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.CurveExtension

open Filter Set
open scoped Topology

variable {E F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
  [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F]

/-- Ambient maps agreeing locally relative to a feasible set have equal actual
derivatives on the velocity of any differentiable curve locally in that set.
The maps need only be genuinely differentiable at the actual curve point. -/
theorem fderiv_eq_on_curve_velocity
    {s : Set E} {f g : E → F} {c : ℝ → E} {t₀ : ℝ} {v : E}
    (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f (c t₀))
    (hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g (c t₀))
    (hc : HasDerivAt c v t₀)
    (hcs : ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝 t₀, c t ∈ s)
    (hfg : f =ᶠ[𝓝[s] (c t₀)] g) :
    fderiv ℝ f (c t₀) v = fderiv ℝ g (c t₀) v := by
  have hcts : Tendsto c (𝓝 t₀) (𝓝[s] (c t₀)) :=
    tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff.mpr ⟨hc.continuousAt, hcs⟩
  have hcomp : (f ∘ c) =ᶠ[𝓝 t₀] (g ∘ c) := hfg.comp_tendsto hcts
  have hfc := hf.hasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt t₀ hc
  have hgc := hg.hasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt t₀ hc
  exact (hfc.congr_of_eventuallyEq hcomp.symm).unique hgc

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.CurveExtension

formulae.label: Selected extension-choice proof edge
formulae.tex: D\bar F(x)[v]=(\bar F\circ c)\prime(0)=(\widehat F\circ c)\prime(0)=D\widehat F(x)[v],\quad c(0)=x,\ c\prime(0)=v.

assumptions: M and M′ are embedded submanifolds of finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces; F:M→M′ is smooth.
F̄ and F̂ are smooth neighborhood extensions of the same F.
Each tangent v at x is represented by a smooth feasible curve c with c(0)=x and c′(0)=v.

obligations.label: Identify the actual manifold differential with the ambient derivative restricted to source tangent vectors, including the target tangent adapter.
Derive linearity and independence from the representing feasible curve.
Derive equality of two actual ambient derivatives on the velocity of a feasible curve from their local agreement.

lesson.title: Why the derivative along a feasible curve ignores the extension
lesson.statement: Let E and V be real normed spaces, s⊆E, and f,g:E→V. At x=c(t₀), suppose f and g are genuinely differentiable, c has actual velocity v, c(t) lies in s for all t sufficiently near t₀, and f=g locally relative to s at x. Then Df(x)[v]=Dg(x)[v].
assumptions: E and V are real normed spaces, possibly infinite-dimensional and incomplete. No chosen Riemannian metric, inner product, Riesz gradient, orthogonal projector or manifold structure is required. This generalizes the finite-dimensional Euclidean source proof ingredient.
Both ambient maps have genuine pointwise Fréchet derivatives at x. Smoothness of the source extensions implies this condition. fderiv is not used to manufacture a derivative when none exists.
c:ℝ→E has a genuine derivative v at t₀ and lies locally in s. Source smooth manifold curves satisfy these weaker local requirements.

The two ambient maps agree on some relative neighborhood of x in s. They need not agree in any open ambient neighborhood. Source neighborhood extensions of the same manifold map supply this equality locally.

steps.title: Pull the agreement back to the curve
steps.text: A differentiable curve is continuous. Together with local feasibility, continuity sends sufficiently small parameter neighborhoods into relative neighborhoods of x in s. The two image curves therefore agree near t₀. This is a local argument: neither extension needs to agree off the feasible set.
steps.lean:
have hcts : Tendsto c (𝓝 t₀) (𝓝[s] (c t₀)) :=
    tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff.mpr ⟨hc.continuousAt, hcs⟩
  have hcomp : (f ∘ c) =ᶠ[𝓝 t₀] (g ∘ c) := hfg.comp_tendsto hcts
steps.detail: HasDerivAt.continuousAt and tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff construct the relative-neighborhood limit. Filter.EventuallyEq.comp_tendsto pulls back local equality.

steps.title: Differentiate each image curve
steps.text: Apply the actual chain rule to each genuinely differentiable ambient map and the actual curve derivative. Its velocity is the ambient derivative applied to v. This derives both image derivatives inside the proof.
steps.lean:
have hfc := hf.hasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt t₀ hc
  have hgc := hg.hasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt t₀ hc
steps.detail: DifferentiableAt.hasFDerivAt gives a real derivative witness; HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt is the Fréchet/one-parameter chain rule.

steps.title: Use locality and uniqueness
steps.text: Locally equal image curves share their derivative at t₀. Transfer the first derivative witness to the second image curve; uniqueness then equates the two velocities. For every source tangent vector represented by a smooth feasible curve, this gives the extension-choice equality. The remaining manifold tangent adapter must be supplied separately.
steps.detail: HasDerivAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq transfers the witness. HasDerivAt.unique compares two genuine derivatives of one image curve.

lesson.lean_statement: DifferentiableAt certifies both ambient derivatives; HasDerivAt certifies the actual curve velocity. Eventually in 𝓝 means locally near t₀. EventuallyEq in 𝓝[s] x means equality on a relative neighborhood. E→V are total Lean function types, but only their local germs enter this proof.
lesson.lean_proof: Pull relative equality back by the continuous feasible curve, apply the two genuine chain rules, then compare derivatives by locality and uniqueness.
